bounds.domain: One immutable organization-credit quote, two competing settlement callers, two customer identities, one original Session and PaymentIntent, one conflicting prior ledger intent, credit value 2, six clock values and a three-tick original dispatch window. Fresh quotes, historical ambiguous rows with missing first-dispatch evidence, and failed historical rows have separate initial states. Provider recovery has up to two pages, an accumulated match, separate scan/failure/conflict/completed states and at most two create dispatches.
bounds.assumptions: Paid/matching is an equivalence class of every immutable receipt check. The provider preserves its request-key contract inside the supported retry window. The primary transaction atomically publishes the order and credit ledger, and uniqueness failure rolls it back. PostgreSQL/PGlite tests independently exercise actual SQL constraints and selected route/service schedules. An empty result authorizes another create only after the complete page traversal; distinct matching Sessions cause a conflict. Each page projects authenticated provider data, not a proof of remote consistency. A second caller may retain an earlier quoted observation and dispatch the same key after the first caller starts; it still must pass the original database time gate, but does not claim a fresh lookup. The lookup invariant applies to an observed recovery state.
bounds.limitations: This component does not establish full checkout refinement. Legacy custom-amount settlement and pack quarantine, arbitrary monetary values, arbitrary provider pagination, pre-provider membership/role withdrawal, multiple orders, refunds/reversals, external request delivery delay and live Stripe behavior require separate composition. No liveness claim: provider, storage or cache can remain unavailable.
